name: Clem Dacey
equipment: Heavy overcoat, charcoal, a size too big since the war, with a torn lining he keeps meaning to fix
.38 revolver, 6 rounds loaded, in a shoulder holster that has worn a shine on his shirt
Blackjack, leather, in the overcoat's inside pocket
Notebook and two pencils, one always broken
Lock picks in a leather fold (a souvenir from a burglary detail)
A pint of rye, half full, in the glove box of a 1938 Plymouth that needs a clutch
Business cards: WALTER DACEY - CONFIDENTIAL INQUIRIES - HOllywood 9-4410, an office over a florist on Cahuenga
A photograph of his kid brother Danny in his Navy whites
features: Plain Dealing (Small-Town origin: +2 Wisdom, +1 Constitution. Once per long rest, an Insight check to tell whether someone is lying is made with advantage, and on a success he also learns whether the lie protects the liar or someone else. Working people start one step friendlier toward him)

Hunch (once per short or long rest, outside combat, ask the GM one yes-or-no question about a lead he has personally encountered in this case and get a true answer; a question on a false premise gets 'wrong question' and the use isn't spent)
Gumshoe (proficiency bonus doubled for Insight and Investigation checks)
Size Them Up (bonus action: study one creature within 60 ft; his next attack against it this turn has advantage and deals an extra 1d6 on a hit; 3 uses (WIS), regained on a short or long rest)

Old Precinct (Ex-Cop background: a desk sergeant will tell him who caught a case, whether a man has a sheet or when a prisoner is moving, for a cup of coffee and a story; some cops remember why he left, Lt. Frank Dolan among them)

personality.traits: I say less than I know and I know less than I'd like. I eat at the same counter every morning and tip the same waitress a quarter, and I notice when anything in a room has moved.
personality.ideals: A client buys my time, not my conscience. When they're the same thing, the client loses.
personality.bonds: My brother Danny. In 1944 he drove drunk into a bus bench on Vine and a man died, and Harlan Shay made it go away, because Danny was a grip at Castellane and I was a cop who could be useful. I have owed Shay ever since. I'd like to stop.
personality.flaws: I can't leave a lie alone, even a kind one, even when leaving it alone is the decent thing.

appearance: Forty-one, long-boned and stooped, with a farmer's big hands and a face like a road map of the San Joaquin Valley. Grey eyes that don't blink enough. A good suit gone shiny at the elbows, an overcoat in all weathers, and a fedora he takes off for women and nobody else.
backstory: Clem Dacey grew up on a raisin farm outside Fresno, came south in 1930 with a dollar and a cardboard suitcase, and joined the LAPD because it was hiring. He made detective in Hollywood Division in 1939 and quit in 1945 when Lieutenant Frank Dolan asked him to find a gun in a suspect's car that wasn't there yet. He has run a one-man agency over a florist on Cahuenga since: divorces, insurance, missing daughters, the occasional studio job. Harlan Shay hired him for this one by name, and Clem knows why: because Clem owes him. He also knows one thing nobody else in the party does. Shay drives a dark green 1941 Packard 180 he is vain about, and Clem has seen its windshield sticker a dozen times in the studio lot: the castle crest and the number seven, because the stickers go by seniority and Shay was there before nearly everyone.
